iter671 — FIX-A: timestamp-minus-timestamp-needs-date_diff inoculation. iter670 Q3 (sessionization 30-min gap) scored 2.50 FLAGGED — the gaps-and-islands STRUCTURE (LAG + running-SUM session_id + COUNT DISTINCT) was correct, but the gap test was written as `event_time - LAG(event_time) OVER (...) > INTERVAL '30' MINUTE`, which is INVALID Trino 467. Per [trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html) verified 2026-06-08: Trino's operator table for temporal types lists ONLY `date - interval -> date`, `time - interval -> time`, `timestamp - interval -> timestamp`, `interval - interval -> interval`. There is NO `timestamp - timestamp -> interval` operator (and NO `date - date -> interval` / `date - date -> integer` operator — same family). The correct idiom is `date_diff('minute', LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time), event_time) > 30` (date_diff returns bigint; compare against a plain integer, NOT an INTERVAL literal). FIX-A generalizes the existing date-minus-date pin (r23:1221+) to also cover timestamp-minus-timestamp, and ADDS a dedicated sessionization canonical at r07 (Pattern B-Session) anchored at the keywords 'session gap', '30 minute gap', 'time between events', 'gap between consecutive events', 'sessionization'.

=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (2026-06-08) ===

WebFetch of trino.io/docs/467/functions/datetime.html:
• Timestamp - Timestamp or Date - Date subtraction: 'Not directly. The documentation shows operators for adding/subtracting intervals from timestamps or dates, but no operator for subtracting two timestamps or dates to get an interval.'
• date_diff signature: `date_diff(unit, timestamp1, timestamp2) -> bigint`. 'Returns timestamp2 - timestamp1 expressed in terms of unit' (such as 'second', 'hour', 'day').
• timestamp + INTERVAL: VALID. Docs example: `timestamp '2012-08-08 01:00' + interval '29' hour` returns `2012-08-09 06:00:00.000`.
• timestamp - INTERVAL: VALID. Docs example: `timestamp '2012-08-08 01:00' - interval '29' hour` returns `2012-08-06 20:00:00.000`.
• Closing recommendation from docs (verbatim): 'If you need to subtract two timestamps, use date_diff() instead of a direct operator.'
